newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Local demand seen braking Russia share correction.
newsitem.headline: Local demand seen braking Russia share correction.

text.p: Leading Russian shares eased on Tuesday on Western selling orders, but traders saw steady Russian support offsetting the selling pressure, leaving the market little changed in the short term.
The Russian Trading System 21-share index ticked down 1.54 percent to 536.31 after closing on Monday at 544.69. Total market turnover was a healthy $76.6 million.
"Today is basically the first day of real Western selling orders. Russians have also lowered their bids somewhat but kept on buying," said one Regent European Securities trader.
"I see the market weak -- it will fall a little bit which is logical after a long rise."
Oil company LUKoil edged down to $26.65 from $27.10 at Monday's close, while local utility Mosenergo slipped to $1.645 from $1.675. Oil company Surgutneftegaz eased to $1.250 from $1.283.
Rinaco-Plus's head of equity trading Andrei Kukk said Russian support was encouraging Western sales.
"Russian clients are buying steadily now and Western clients are steadily selling," Kukk said. "It is clear that Western banks, who want to see a fall of three percent a day, are the winners."
Traders saw stocks correcting further in parallel with Western markets spooked by volatility on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones index had not fully recovered Friday's sharp loss.
"Banks are over-estimating their strength in buying so doggedly, since market growth has been fairly prolonged and strong and in the West the trend has already turned," said Kukk.
"Russia is too well integrated into the world economy not to take notice of that."
But Russian demand would cushion the fall, traders said.
"The market is fairly solid and the money -- mainly Russian -- in it is enough to avoid sharp fluctuations," Kukk said.
